---
title: "Resources: CAPA — root cause to effectiveness check"
order: 18
---

Each link below was checked this session and loads.

- **[21 CFR 606.100 — Cornell Legal Information Institute](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/606.100)**
  — the SOP and investigation regulation. Paragraph (c)'s "conclusions and followup" sentence is
  this module's regulatory floor under root cause analysis. Local verbatim copy:
  `sources/cfr/606.100.md`.

- **[21 CFR 606.171 — Cornell Legal Information Institute](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/606.171)**
  — the biological product deviation reporting rule. Paragraph (f)'s "should be investigated"
  language, quoted in this lesson, is a rare example of guidance-tier wording inside an otherwise
  "must"-heavy regulation. Local copy: `sources/cfr/606.171.md`.

- **[GovInfo: Code of Federal Regulations collection](https://www.govinfo.gov/app/collection/cfr)**
  — the U.S. Government Publishing Office's official CFR collection. Use it as a fallback primary
  source if eCFR or Cornell is ever unreachable, or to pull an official PDF of a full CFR part for
  the record.

- **[What Is a CAPA? From Root Cause to Effectiveness Check | Matrix
  Quality](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5841rTtAIVs)** (Matrix One, from oEmbed `author_name`) —
  the video embedded in this lesson. Matrix One is a QMS (quality management system) software
  vendor producing educational content; this is a general industry explainer of the same
  root-cause-to-effectiveness-check arc this lesson teaches, not tied to AABB, FDA, or any CFR
  citation here — useful for hearing the same four-stage shape argued from outside the
  blood-specific lens. Verified embeddable via YouTube oEmbed on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[MindTools: 5 Whys](https://www.mindtools.com/a3mi00v/5-whys)** — a well-regarded management-
  skills publication's walkthrough of the 5 Whys technique this lesson runs on Brookfield's event,
  including the discipline of keeping each "why" aimed at the process rather than a person. ASQ's
  own public page on 5 Whys returned an HTTP 403 to this session's automated requests again this
  time (a bot-blocking response, not a broken page) — this is the different source this module
  went looking for in its place. **Verification note:** this link returned HTTP 200 on first
  check but HTTP 403 on independent re-check — inconsistent, bot-protection-style behavior, the
  same pattern this curriculum has already seen from eCFR, FDA, and CDC pages. Likely reachable
  in a real browser; not reliably confirmed with an automated fetch this session.

- **[TechTarget: Fishbone diagram](https://www.techtarget.com/whatis/definition/fishbone-diagram)**
  — a technology-publication explainer on the fishbone (Ishikawa) diagram, the alternative root-
  cause tool this lesson names for messier events with several plausible contributing branches
  instead of Brookfield's one clean chain. Useful for seeing that tool argued on its own terms
  before you need it on a real multi-branch CAPA. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11
  (HTTP 200, after a redirect).

- **[Pharmaceutical Online: A SMART Approach To CAPA Effectiveness
  Checks](https://www.pharmaceuticalonline.com/doc/a-smart-approach-to-capa-effectiveness-checks-0001)**
  — an industry publication's guest column on designing a CAPA effectiveness check that can
  actually fail: writing the measurable criterion, time window, and data source before you check,
  the same discipline this lesson applies to Lakeshore's six-month document-control re-audit. Use
  this before writing a real effectiveness-check criterion of your own. Verified loading via
  `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[Quality Digest: Why Do Most CAPAs
  Fail?](https://www.qualitydigest.com/inside/qms-and-standards-article/why-do-most-capas-fail-051926.html)**
  — an industry quality publication on the common ways a CAPA file collapses — closing on
  implementation instead of effectiveness, "human error" standing in for root cause, no
  independent re-check — the same traps this lesson's "Common traps" section names for Lakeshore,
  argued from general industry experience rather than this module's own scenario. Verified
  loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200, after a redirect to the article's current URL).
